events.title: Pierre and Marie Curie isolate radium
events.description: In their Paris laboratory, the Curies succeeded in isolating radium, a new radioactive element, after years of painstaking work on tonnes of pitchblende ore.
events.significance: The discovery opened the door to modern research on radioactivity and to radiation therapy for cancer. It earned the Curies a share of the 1903 Nobel Prize in Physics.

events.title: Birth of painter Joan Miró
events.description: Joan Miró was born in Barcelona, Spain. He became one of the 20th century's most distinctive artists, known for playful, dreamlike forms and vivid colour.
events.significance: Miró helped define Surrealism and left a lasting mark on modern painting, sculpture and ceramics.

events.title: Columbine High School massacre
events.description: Two students opened fire at Columbine High School near Denver, Colorado. They killed 13 people and then themselves, and wounded 24 others.
events.significance: The attack shocked the world. It reshaped school safety practices in the United States and sparked lasting debate about gun violence and prevention.

events.title: Deepwater Horizon rig explodes
events.description: An explosion on the Deepwater Horizon drilling platform in the Gulf of Mexico killed 11 workers. The rig was operated by Transocean for BP.
events.significance: The blast led to the largest accidental marine oil spill in history. It caused severe environmental damage and prompted major changes in offshore drilling regulation.
